result:
The perpetual notion that life dances in the rhythm we provide is a fascinating one. After all, isn't life a spectrum of choices and forks in roads that lead us to the person we are, the person we were, and the person we aspire to be? We set aspiring goals for ourselves, picking up different life-mantras and then embrace or discard them based on personal vagaries. We journey through the continuum of life with a borrowed hope and optimism, capable of surpassing the trivial illnesses of life that threaten to plague our existence. 

It all starts in the throes of childhood, where we excitedly explore worlds within worlds, galaxies within pinpricks of stars. Life is an endless playground, curiosity the gleaming halo surrounding our innocent heads. There is no excess baggage of past disappointments or worries for the future. There is only the now, the present, that presents itself to us with a child-like enthusiasm. A time where questions are many and answers are sought with an insatiable thirst. The world is the grand canvas on which we paint our fantasies and dreams.

As we journey forward into adolescence, our heady dreams gradually tone down, but the zeal remains. Forever buried in textbooks, life oscillates between a mathematics problem and an elusive poem like a pendulum, trying to find a balance. Everything is heightened, felt more vividly; the first rush of love, the sting of a first broken heart. We start grappling with the human dichotomy that we are as individuals, fluctuating between conformity and rebellion, insight and ignorance, paradoxes that nature had so wonderfully engineered into us. We now see the world not just as a toy-box full of shiny objects but also as a labyrinth of choices and possibilities, understanding the beauty in chaos.

Then comes adulthood, where life is no longer lived in the multitude of a playground but in the confines of cubicles. The world looks different from childhood. The buildings seem taller, and the stars distant. Logic triumphs over imagination, reality tinges our dreams. Suddenly, there is a rush of responsibilities. It is not just about self anymore; it is about family, about children, about society. Our passions often give way to practicality. Yet, it is also a time where we understand more profoundly, love more deeply, and grow resilient against life's recovery assaults. Our notions and beliefs rock solid, accepting our flaws while striving to be the best versions of ourselves.

As twilight years approach, life slows down like a languid river. We have tasted life's sweet wine and aged alongside it. Patterns emerge from chaos, coherence from randomness. The smaller pleasures of life bring joy, while the elusive pursuit of fame and fortune matters little. Family and love hold a different meaning; they become the heart which, when pressed against the ear, unfolds the sweetest melody of life. We watch the world around us change, talking to us in languages we now thoroughly understand. The sight of children brings a nostalgic smile, adults a remembering nod, the world, a lifetime of understanding. We become the poets, the philosophers, the scholars studying the complex abstraction of life.

At the end of it all, perhaps life is a wonderful tapestry of these stages, of millions of individual instances knit together. It is a carnival, a circus, and a tranquil library all at once. The beauty of life's absurdity and simplicity, its ruthless cruelty, and compassionate grace are all experiences that make us, us. 

Despite all its ups and downs, the uncertainties, the changes, life remains the most fantastic jouissance. It is to be lived, to be laughed, to be cried, and to be loved. It is to experience the warmth of the sunlight on a chilly morning, the tranquil silence of the night, the first drops of rain on parched soil, and savor the bold strokes of nature's grand canvas. Life is a masterpiece, crafted by the divine and rendered to us; we only strive to seek its meaning through our relatable experiences. 

To make oneself wholesome is to ride on this journey accepting its ebbs and flows, at times hurriedly, at times stopping to smell the flowers, savor the moments, toast to the years passed, and to the years yet to come. It is to find glimmers of happiness even in the most dismal moments, to desire, to aspire, to fall and rise, to fail and succeed. This, perhaps, is the true essence of life, a saga of growth, a ballad of survival, a sonnet to love, and an ode to hope, one that enthralls us and leaves us wanting more.
